title: The Wheel Options Strategy | My NEW Credo Technology (CRDO) Trading Plan 2026 - Options With Ryan

steps.does: Shows the public portfolio account screen and says it is trading near all-time highs.
steps.why: Establish credibility of the wheel results before teaching it.

steps.does: Opens the realized gain/loss page, reads current-year profits, then switches to the previous calendar year.
steps.why: Show the wheel strategy has produced realized profits in both years.
steps.conclusion: Strategy has worked well for him in both years, though results vary.

steps.does: Opens CRDO chart, notes the move from $46 in mid 2025 to about $218, draws a line from 18 months ago to now, scrolls further back, and contrasts with Lululemon's downtrend since 2024.
steps.why: Make sure assigned shares are likely to recover and rise; reject downtrending stocks.
steps.conclusion: CRDO passes; Lululemon would fail for the wheel.

steps.does: Quotes forward P/E about 30 and trailing P/E about 70, then shows TradingView's P/E ratio pane at about 78 and notes it was 200+ when the stock was $76.
steps.why: Confirm profitability and that earnings growth is lowering valuation.
steps.conclusion: Meets the positive, under-100 P/E requirement.

steps.does: States CRDO has five straight earnings beats and zero misses.
steps.why: Earnings consistency protects against a downward trend after assignment.

steps.does: Goes through a fundamentals slide: revenue $1.3B, cash $1.4B, gross margin 67-69%, net margin above 50%, projected 114% revenue growth, then shows bull $320-350, neutral $265-280 and bear cases.
steps.why: Judge whether the company deserves a place on his approved list.
steps.conclusion: CRDO is on the approved list.

rules.text: Stock must have been in an upward-trending chart for the past year and a half.
P/E must be positive, ideally under 100; if over 100 the company needs enough cash to cover its debts.
Requires at least 2.5% premium on a 30-day, 30-delta put.
Requires consistent earnings beats every quarter.

steps.does: Shows a slide of VIX bands and a TradingView VIX chart with Bollinger-style bands, explains VIX as the fear index, and places the current VIX around 15-17 in the slight-fear band.
steps.why: Decide how much cash to hold on the sidelines for better entries.
steps.conclusion: Keep 20-25% cash and 75-80% invested; not too cash heavy because low VIX can persist for months.

steps.does: Caps CRDO at 10% of the portfolio via cash-secured puts; with a $200K account that allows about one put (about $20K assignment).
steps.why: Keep any single assignment at or below 10% of the portfolio.
steps.conclusion: Only one put on a $200K account.

rules.text: Do not go all in when the VIX is very low; keep cash (about 20-25% at VIX 15-20).
Never allocate more than 10% of the portfolio to a single stock via cash-secured puts.

steps.does: States the setup: 25-30 days to expiration (up to 35), 25-30 delta, drop to 20 delta or lower for safety, hold to expiration or roll up if 80% profit with about 20 days left.
steps.why: Stay inside the 60-day theta decay window; far-dated puts do not pay for the time risk.
data: roll at 80% profit with ~20 days left
steps.conclusion: 30 days and 25-30 delta is his standard.

steps.does: Opens the CRDO chain for October 30th (28 days), clicks the 200 strike bid to see the mid price of $935 (about 4.9% ROI at roughly 29 delta), and compares with the 190 strike (21 delta, about $560) and 185 strike.
steps.why: Higher delta means more premium but more assignment risk; lower delta means less premium and less risk.
steps.conclusion: Picks around 190 (21 delta) or 185 for safer assignment distance; 25 delta is typical these days.

steps.does: Notes CRDO trading near the upper Bollinger band after a two-week run, and that it breached the lower band before and snapped back in.
steps.why: Judge whether to take a safer strike given the stock's elevated position and volatility.
steps.conclusion: A bit more risk here, so he leans toward the safer 185-190 strike.

rules.text: Stay within about 25-35 days to expiration; do not sell far-dated puts because time decay does not pay for the risk.
Typical delta is 25-30; go to 20 or lower for caution.

steps.does: Uses a hypothetical assignment at $215 with stock at $218, opens a 21-day chain, compares the 30-delta 245 strike (about $685, near 3% premium plus about 10% appreciation) with a strike only $5 above 220 (about $1,200, over 6% premium).
steps.why: Hit the 2.5-5% monthly target while keeping some appreciation.
steps.conclusion: Prefers the 30-delta strike for premium plus appreciation; if cost basis cannot be cleared go 40-50 days out.

rules.text: Never sell a covered call below the assignment price.
If the strike cannot be above assignment price, go further out in time (about 40-50 days).
